_what: SANE verdicts, adopted from scripts/sane_proposals.md. This file is the hold-back gate's ONLY source: a registry widget bakes into slot 1 only where its chapter's verdict is >= the bar. Below it, or absent, the widget slot is skipped and the concept resolves down the precedence chain.
_confirmation: confirmed: adopt scripts/sane_proposals.md as SANE verdicts for the chapters it covers, verdict_by raasikh; precompute all chapters with hold-back below 85%
_why_a_file_and_not_a_column: The directive asks for SANE COLUMNS. There is no sane table or column in the database — verified against the live schema, not assumed. Creating them is a migration, and CC never applies migrations. migrations/0046_sane_verdicts.sql is written and NOT applied; Raasikh runs it, and once the columns exist this file is what backfills them. Until then the gate reads this, so the hold-back is enforceable now rather than pending.
_unmeasured_is_not_a_pass: A chapter absent from `verdicts` is UNMEASURED, and unmeasured is held back exactly like a failing score. The recurring defect in this project is a check that passes on absent information; treating 'no verdict' as 'fine' would be that defect wearing a policy's clothes.

verdicts.subject: physics
verdicts.note: Two of the ten proposed-n rows were HARD errors fixed in Session F (gauss seg3 point->gaussian_cylinder for an infinite line charge; gauss seg4 parallel_plates->gaussian_pillbox for a single sheet). Re-scoring on that alone would give 32/40 = 80.0%, still short of the bar. The verdict recorded here is the proposals' own number, as adopted — not a figure I recomputed after my own fixes.

verdicts.subject: mathematics
verdicts.note: The furthest from the bar by a wide margin. 16 of the 40 are fired-widget parameter faults, 15 are wrong-picture choices.

verdicts.subject: chemistry
verdicts.note: The closest any chapter comes, and it still does not clear. batch6/DIRECTIVE.md states this chapter at 89.4%; the proposals file it cites says 83.2% (94 of 113). The file is the source that was adopted, so 83.2 is the verdict. 89.4 would have cleared the bar and 83.2 does not, so the difference decides whether chem's widgets bake.

verdicts.subject: biology
verdicts.note: The proposals give two framings: the in-sheet 40 rows at 70.0% and the full 70 measured at 75.7%. The larger sample is recorded. Both sit below the bar, so the hold-back is identical either way and the choice changes nothing.
